regime_context: Detector shows Banks as the sole eligible (trend-gate passing) theme with the highest durability bar (0.75) and positive breadth (0.611), but rotation breadth is extremely narrow (1 of 22 themes eligible) and the backtest verdict flags that the absolute-trend gate did NOT hold on this market's history — it mean-reverts and whipsaws the gate. So the one validated drawdown edge is absent here; everything else is coincident and momentum rank-IC is ~0. This is a display-only, low-conviction regime.
emerging_watch: Watching Banks' breadth erosion as an early sign the one-narrative is aging: if Banks' breadth (0.611) decays below 0.35 while Gold Miners gains breadth above 0.2 and becomes eligible, that would retire this watch and mark a confirmed leadership handoff — otherwise the narrow single-theme regime persists.

theses.subject: Banks
theses.thesis: Banks is the only theme passing the absolute-trend gate (eligible=true) and holds the top momentum rank with the highest durability bar (0.75) and breadth (0.611), indicating leadership is broad and cohesive rather than a one-stock spike. However, because gate_helps is false on this market (mean-reverting tape whipsaws the trend gate), the trend discipline itself has no validated drawdown edge here, so the lean is a directional tilt toward the prevailing narrative, not an extracted edge.
theses.dissent: Crowding flag (z=1.6, crowded=true) and the fact that gate_helps=false mean the trend gate historically does not cut drawdown on China A-shares; a mean-reverting tape could whipsaw the bank leader, and crowding marks attention tops in this market's history.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners ranks #2 on momentum (score 0.677) but is ineligible (trend gate fails) with low durability bar (0.31) and zero breadth (0.0). theses.dissent: Gold miners can act as a flight-to-safety hedge against the macro backdrop of geopolitical headlines and 100% unscheduled surprise share; its rank #2 momentum could persist even without the trend gate.
